definitions.explanation: A forest with very thick, closely packed vegetation. Often refers to tropical jungles or any heavily wooded area that is difficult to penetrate.

examples.japanese: {密林|みつりん}を{探検|たんけん}する。
アマゾンの{密林|みつりん}には{未知|みち}の{生物|せいぶつ}がいる。
examples.english: There are unknown creatures in the Amazon jungle.

examples.japanese: {密林|みつりん}の{奥|おく}に{分|わ}け{入|い}ると、{巨大|きょだい}な{滝|たき}が{姿|すがた}を{現|あらわ}した。
examples.english: When we pushed deep into the jungle, a massive waterfall came into view.

notes:
Composed of {密|みつ} (dense, thick) + {林|りん} (forest, woods). Evokes an image of lush, impenetrable vegetation. In modern Japanese slang, {密林|みつりん} is sometimes used as a nickname for Amazon (the company), playing on the meaning 'jungle.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {密林|みつりん}を{探検|たんけん}する: to explore the jungle
- {密林|みつりん}の{奥|おく}: deep in the jungle
- {熱帯|ねったい}{密林|みつりん}: tropical jungle
- {密林|みつりん}{地帯|ちたい}: jungle zone

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ジャングル: jungle (loanword; more casual and common in everyday speech)
- {森林|しんりん}: forest (general term; not necessarily dense)
- {原生林|げんせいりん}: virgin forest, old-growth forest (emphasis on being untouched)
